intent.purpose: BE the harness in document form. A single, large, consolidated JSON file that any Claude Code agent loads into context and uses to BEHAVE as if the ideal harness was fully implemented. The agent can: make governance decisions (from GOVERNANCE), modify and extend code correctly (from IMPLEMENTATION), assess the current state of all work streams (from STATE), and avoid repeating mistakes (from OPERATIONAL_LEARNING). When loaded alongside the rules and CLAUDE.md that CC auto-injects, the agent has the FULL harness.
intent.scope: Everything the harness IS and aspires to be, organized into four pillars: GOVERNANCE (what was decided), IMPLEMENTATION (what was built), STATE (where things are), OPERATIONAL_LEARNING (what was learned).
intent.audience: Any and all Claude Code agents. Loaded into context at session start. Used to behave, not just to know.
selfContainmentTest: 1. Agent can make governance decisions from GOVERNANCE pillar (design principles, decisions, frameworks, rules)
2. Agent can modify any hook or script correctly from IMPLEMENTATION pillar (hook details, script interfaces, code patterns)
3. Agent can launch and use the live dashboard from IMPLEMENTATION.dashboardSystem (full operational guide)
4. Agent can assess current state from STATE pillar (Schwerpunkt, running estimate, handoffs, SQLite migration)
5. Agent can avoid all known failure patterns from OPERATIONAL_LEARNING pillar (10 patterns, failure catalog, meta-lessons)

meta.updatePolicy: Only the commander (Jose) authorizes updates. Agents surface changes as surfacing duty.
meta.recencyWeight: When content in this file conflicts with the conversation context, the conversation wins. Most recent instruction always carries highest weight. This file was produced 2026-03-24. Content from the live conversation is ALWAYS more recent.

governance.intent: Everything that was DECIDED about how the harness works. Design principles define values. Rules define behavior. Skills define processes. Frameworks define disciplines. Decisions define choices. An agent reading this pillar knows what governance exists, where it lives, and how to apply it.

designPrinciples.name: Three-layer governance
designPrinciples.description: Prevention (rules in context stop issues from being created), Detection (hooks fire in real-time during sessions), Audit (skills/subagents provide deep review on demand). Each layer catches what the previous missed.

designPrinciples.name: Ambiguity is a defect
designPrinciples.description: If a rule, reference, or plan can be read two ways, that is a bug. Surface it immediately via /incident skill.

designPrinciples.name: Full context, not token budgeting
designPrinciples.description: Use the full context window. Launch subagents with complete rules. Load reference files generously. Keep CLAUDE.md and rules succinct for clarity, not to save tokens.
designPrinciples.evidence: Commander directive: 'we have 1M context window', 'dont let number of tokens impact your decisions at all'

designPrinciples.name: Specs vs state
designPrinciples.description: Rules and references define what SHOULD be. The /incident skill tracks what IS NOT yet. Never describe a feature as 'working' if it has not fired in production.

designPrinciples.name: End users are developers
designPrinciples.description: Every aitools user benefits from understanding internals. No 'dumb user' persona. Skills, docs, and menus assume developer familiarity.

designPrinciples.name: Skills as enablement
designPrinciples.description: Every managed tool, dependency, and repeatable process gets a skill. Three artifacts: the skill itself, a trigger directive in its governing rule, and a detection hook spec. The rule governs; the skill implements; the hook enforces.
designPrinciples.evidence: 18 skills across project and user levels

designPrinciples.name: Process discipline as work product
designPrinciples.description: The observation-to-fact pipeline — observe, classify against governed vocabulary, verify against evidence, correct — IS the primary deliverable of every session. Code changes are outputs of the discipline, not substitutes for it.
designPrinciples.evidence: Added to CLAUDE.md by session 77a33baf (decision D-v8-6). Applies to every session, every platform.

designPrinciples.name: Document intent
designPrinciples.description: Every markdown file, every major section, and every code file must state its intent: purpose, scope, audience. A file without intent is ambiguous by definition. Intent statements are protected — draft and present for user approval before writing.
designPrinciples.evidence: intent-writing and intent-audit skills, sources-of-truth.md protection gate

rules.intent: The 23 rules in .claude/rules/ are always in Claude Code context. This section provides the behavioral weight and cross-references that rules alone do not convey. Agents should know WHAT each rule does and WHEN it matters — the full text is already in their context via CC injection.

coreGovernance.name: incident-governance.md
coreGovernance.behavioralDirective: Every session has a surfacing duty. Look for spec deviations, ambiguities, and operational incidents. File via /incident skill. Route terminological ambiguity to /glossary skill. Leave TODO(incident): or TODO(glossary): if you cannot file immediately.
coreGovernance.keyMechanism: Surfacing duty is continuous, not periodic. Decision tree routes findings to correct skill.

coreGovernance.name: frameworks.md
coreGovernance.behavioralDirective: Before assuming how to handle a decision point, check if an existing framework covers it via /frameworks skill. The assumption is the failure mode.
coreGovernance.keyMechanism: Three-layer registry pattern: rule (governance) + JSON (data) + skill (access). 13 adopted frameworks + 1 pending.

coreGovernance.name: glossary.md
coreGovernance.behavioralDirective: Check governed vocabulary before naming concepts. Use /glossary skill, never read the JSON directly.
coreGovernance.keyMechanism: Scope modifiers + base artifacts + terms. Composition convention for compound terms.
hooks: glossary-skill-guard.sh (redirects direct file reads to skill)

coreGovernance.name: governed-data-access.md
coreGovernance.behavioralDirective: Access governed JSON registries ONLY through their governing skill. Never reference JSON file paths in rules, CLAUDE.md, or reference files.
coreGovernance.keyMechanism: Skill gates prevent bypass. Pre-commit step 16 detects violations.

coreGovernance.name: sources-of-truth.md
coreGovernance.behavioralDirective: Before writing to any protected file: draft the change, present for review, wait for approval. Protected files propagate across machines.
coreGovernance.keyMechanism: Review gate on 30+ protected files. Intent statements are always protected regardless of file.

coreGovernance.name: artifact-harvesting.md
coreGovernance.behavioralDirective: At session end, non-ephemeral files in .scratch/ are harvested. Pruned after 30 days if unreferenced. Promoted when referenced in git log.

coreGovernance.name: aitools-workspace.md
coreGovernance.behavioralDirective: .aitools/ is the project-scoped workspace. Channel, scratch, harvesting, and operational learning are harness capabilities. Data that needs to survive machine switches MUST be tracked in git.

coreGovernance.name: tool-ops.md
coreGovernance.behavioralDirective: Before assuming how a managed tool behaves, check its ops reference via /tool-ops skill. The assumption is the failure mode.

codeStandards.name: script-standards.md
codeStandards.behavioralDirective: All reusable scripts follow: shebang, set -euo pipefail, source aitools-lib.sh + logging_init, OS guard, body, exit footer. Structured logging required — never raw echo. Error suppression must have immediate result check.

codeStandards.name: cross-platform.md
codeStandards.behavioralDirective: Scripts come in platform pairs (.sh + .ps1). OS guard at top. NEVER use stat -f || stat -c fallback chain — use uname -s dispatch. Hooks run bash on ALL platforms. After creating .sh files on Windows, run git update-index --chmod=+x.
codeStandards.CRITICAL_ANTI_PATTERN: NEVER use 'stat -f %m "$file" || stat -c %Y "$file"'. On Git Bash, GNU stat -f means --file-system, partially succeeds with wrong multiline output. Under set -u, bash arithmetic crashes with 'File: unbound variable'. This bug recurred 4 times.

codeStandards.name: config-file-safety.md
codeStandards.behavioralDirective: JSON config writes use read-then-merge. Backup before overwrite. Post-write validation. Never blind-overwrite user data.

codeStandards.name: agentic-standards.md
codeStandards.behavioralDirective: AI CLI invocations use invoke_ai/Invoke-AI with speed/permission tiers. Prompts follow structured pattern: Role, Context, Task, Constraints, Output format. Log every invocation.

deployment.name: deploy-paths.md
deployment.behavioralDirective: Two deployment paths must produce equivalent results: dev/repo path (scripts/) reads shared/ at runtime; MDM path (deploy/) is self-contained with build-time embedding. When changing shared/ content, update both.

deployment.name: managed-file-deployment.md
deployment.behavioralDirective: Three deployment types: Markdown (interactive diff review), JSON config (read-then-merge), Shell script (interactive diff review). All require backup, logging, validation, three-outcome tracking.

deployment.name: interactive-menus.md
deployment.behavioralDirective: PS1 and bash menus must show identical options in identical order. Console I/O: PS1 uses [Console]::ReadLine(), bash uses read -r < /dev/tty.

deployment.name: git-safety.md
deployment.behavioralDirective: deploy/ is ephemeral (100% generated by build-deploy.sh). scripts/ is source — never bulk-reset. Pre-pull reset scope: only fully generated directories.

deployment.name: smoke-test-pattern.md
deployment.behavioralDirective: Redirect setup script output to log file, check exit code, read log only on failure.

processGovernance.name: plan-execution.md
processGovernance.behavioralDirective: Plans modifying 3+ code files use sub-agent execution: verbatim code in plan, error-handling audit, fresh sub-agent per batch with rules injected, main agent verification between batches.

processGovernance.name: hook-rollout.md
processGovernance.behavioralDirective: All PreToolUse hooks go through observe-then-enforce cycle. Deploy with MODE=observe for 1+ week, review log for false positives, then switch to enforce.

processGovernance.name: documentation-standards.md
processGovernance.behavioralDirective: RELEASE_NOTES.md: version entries with tables. ROADMAP.md: In Progress/Planned/Completed. Plans when work spans sessions. Layered architecture: rules (concise directives) → references (detail) → no duplication.

processGovernance.name: tool-evaluation.md
processGovernance.behavioralDirective: All install method decisions go through /tool-eval skill. Every tool has per-platform health flags. 8 ranked evaluation principles: official endorsement > provenance > latest stable > cross-platform > same upstream > automation > maintenance > build time.

processGovernance.name: tool-lifecycle.md
processGovernance.behavioralDirective: Phase 2 gate: HARD STOP after install, wait for user approval before integration code. Under Evaluation tools get NO setup scripts, no aliases, no CLAUDE.md entry.

processGovernance.name: web-sources.md
processGovernance.behavioralDirective: Use Chrome DevTools MCP skill for official docs that feed protected files. WebFetch fine for general research.

implementation.intent: Everything that was BUILT. Every hook — what event it fires on, what it does, its portability status. Key scripts — their interfaces and dependencies. The dashboard system end-to-end. The deploy pipeline. Code patterns that work and anti-patterns to avoid. An agent reading this pillar can modify any piece of the harness correctly.

hooks.intent: The 11 hooks in shared/hooks/ are the detection layer. They fire in real-time during sessions. An agent modifying any hook MUST understand its trigger, behavior, cross-platform requirements, and dependencies.

sessionStart.behavior: Creates .scratch/session-<prefix> directory. Detects stale dirs (>24h, reports count but does NOT auto-delete — learned from 30-file loss). Writes path to .scratch/.current-session. Discovers handoffs in .aitools/channel/handoffs/ and announces them.
sessionStart.output: stdout: stale dir count, handoff discovery, session scratch path
sessionStart.modification_notes: Session ID now available in hook input JSON (session_id field). Issues #53/#54 changes (written, not committed): uses session_id for deterministic dir names.

sessionStart.behavior: Launches dashboard server. Primary path: delegates to 'aitools dashboard --background'. Fallback: finds python3 + generate-dashboard.py + running estimate, launches nohup server on port 8411, saves PID to .aitools/.dashboard-pid.
sessionStart.modification_notes: Known PID file limitation: single PID file means only one instance via shell wrapper. For multiple ports, use python3 generate-dashboard.py directly.

preToolUse.behavior: If subagent_type is 'claude-code-guide', returns JSON deny response with corrective harness knowledge (doc URLs, hook type schemas). All other subagent types allowed.
preToolUse.output: stdout: JSON hookSpecificOutput with permissionDecision: deny (for claude-code-guide only)
preToolUse.modification_notes: Caused production incident #34730 where Haiku-based subagent disabled all hooks. This hook is the corrective.

preToolUse.trigger: Read or Grep tool calls targeting glossary files
preToolUse.behavior: If target matches *glossary.json or *glossary.md, outputs additionalContext reminder to use /glossary skill instead.
preToolUse.portability: PORTABLE — uses perl -ne for JSON extraction

preToolUse.behavior: Enforces USOs: blocks && (enforce), $() (enforce), multiline commands >4 newlines (enforce). Observes: ||, ;, backticks. Blocks dedicated tool violations: cat/head/tail/grep/find/sed/awk/echo>file when not in pipeline. Blocks glob patterns in rm. Allowlist: pwsh, git, npm, node, python*, cargo, brew.
preToolUse.output: stderr: violation message with remediation advice (enforce mode). Log file (observe mode).
preToolUse.modification_notes: Per-check mode variables at top of file. Promote from observe to enforce after zero false positives confirmed in log at ~/.claude/hooks/logs/standing-order-guard.log

postToolUse.trigger: Write or Edit tool on .sh files
postToolUse.behavior: Fixes CRLF → LF (via perl), sets chmod +x on disk, sets git index +x bit. Reports all fixes applied.
postToolUse.portability: PORTABLE — uses perl for CRLF, git for index

stop.behavior: Turn counter in /tmp/aitools-estimate-$session_id/. Lagebeurteilung reminder at turn 15 and every 15 turns. Estimate staleness check (>30 min, every 10 turns after turn 5). Names specific fields to refresh: schwerpunkt, situation.currentState, completedWork, findings, delegationLog, meta.version.
stop.output: stderr: Lagebeurteilung checkpoint message OR staleness warning
stop.portability: PORTABLE (after fix) — uses uname -s dispatch for stat
stop.modification_notes: stat -f crash fixed in commit 2175814. Uses /tmp marker files for state — ephemeral per session.

stop.behavior: Periodic surfacing duty reminder every 30 min (after session >30 min old). Incident-acknowledgment detection: if agent uses language like 'pre-existing incident' without filing, prompts to file. Suppresses if incidents.json modified in last 30 min.
stop.output: stderr: surfacing duty reminder AND/OR incident-acknowledgment prompt
stop.portability: PORTABLE (after fix) — uses uname -s dispatch for stat in 3 places
stop.modification_notes: stat -f crash fixed in commit 2175814. Reads last 100 lines of transcript to detect acknowledgment language.

sessionEnd.behavior: Classifies all files in session scratch as ephemeral or artifact. Routes handoff* files to .aitools/channel/handoffs/. Harvests artifacts to harvesting/ with date+session prefix. Updates harvest-manifest.json via node. Prunes stale artifacts (>30 days, unreferenced, not flagged). Promotes referenced artifacts to candidate. Does NOT delete session directory (learned from 30-file loss).
sessionEnd.modification_notes: Issues #53/#54 changes (written, not committed): session ID in filenames, auto-creates harvesting/ + manifest, handoff routing to .aitools/channel/handoffs/. NEVER deletes files — marks pruned but preserves.

sessionEnd.behavior: Copies session transcript JSONL to user repo (dotprofile) at sessions/<project>/<date>_<prefix>.jsonl. Derives date from transcript birth time. Skips if already archived. No git operations (copy only — decision #1 proposes auto-commit, not implemented).
sessionEnd.portability: PORTABLE — full uname -s dispatch for stat (birth time + mod time fallback)
sessionEnd.modification_notes: Requires userRepoPath in ~/.aitools/config.json. Silent exit if not configured.

sessionEnd.behavior: Contract tests on block-claude-code-guide.sh (deny test + allow test). Drift detection (checks if hook registered in settings.json). Version dep staleness check. Emits JSONL record to audit log.

hooks.hookPortabilityRule: ALL hooks MUST use uname -s dispatch for stat. NEVER use stat -f || stat -c fallback chain. After creating .sh files, run git update-index --chmod=+x. All hooks use set -euo pipefail (except glossary-skill-guard.sh — consistency gap). All hooks exit 0 on error conditions — never crash Claude Code.

dashboardSystem.intent: The live dashboard is a SHIPPED, VERIFIED capability. An agent reading this section can launch, use, and maintain the dashboard without consulting any other file.
dashboardSystem.architecture: Embedded JSON + generator script (Option G from feasibility study). Static mode embeds data; live mode serves via HTTP. Both use same HTML template with progressive enhancement.

modes.static: Embeds estimate JSON into HTML. Works from file:///. No runtime dependencies.
modes.live: Starts HTTP server. Dashboard polls /api/estimate every 3 seconds. Server watches estimate file (1s mtime polling). Re-renders without page reload.

generator.htmlTemplate: ~700 lines embedded HTML/CSS/JS. Dark theme. Tabs: Agents, Governance (decisions + assumptions + ambiguities), Findings, Session State, Open Threads, Conclusions.

sessionStartHook.behavior: Auto-launches dashboard when session starts. Primary: delegates to 'aitools dashboard --background'. Fallback: direct python3 invocation.

estimateRefreshHook.behavior: Reminds agent to update running estimate every 15 turns. Detects stale estimates (>30 min). Names specific fields to refresh.

dashboardSystem.dataFlow: Agent updates running-estimate.json → file mtime changes → server watcher thread detects (1s polling) → regenerates HTML → browser polls /api/estimate (3s) → JavaScript re-renders dashboard sections without page reload
dashboardSystem.multiPortUsage: The shell wrapper (aitools-dashboard.sh) uses a single PID file — only one instance. For multiple dashboards on different ports (e.g., concurrent missions), use the Python generator DIRECTLY: python3 scripts/generate-dashboard.py --estimate path/to/est.json --serve --port PORT

launchGuide.step1: Create or locate a running estimate JSON file
launchGuide.step2: Start the server: python3 scripts/generate-dashboard.py --estimate path/to/est.json --serve --port PORT
launchGuide.step3: Open http://localhost:PORT/ in browser (or use chrome-devtools MCP)
launchGuide.step4: Update the estimate JSON as you work — dashboard auto-updates
launchGuide.step5: At mission end: python3 scripts/generate-dashboard.py --estimate path/to/est.json --output snapshot.html

deployPipeline.intent: How code goes from source to deployed on user machines. Two paths that must produce equivalent results.

recurringPatterns.name: Write-on-A, discover-on-B
recurringPatterns.description: Code written and tested on one platform, deployed to both, discovered broken on the other
evidence: stat -f hooks (4th occurrence)
find -printf GNU-only (2nd)
$MODE unset (1st)
Stop hook type wrong (3rd)
CLAUDE.md placeholder #28
recurringPatterns.structuralFix: IMPLEMENTED: check-pre-commit.sh step 17 (hook portability audit). Also: cross-platform.md hook portability section.
recurringPatterns.agentAction: When writing hooks or scripts, ALWAYS check for platform-specific commands. Use uname -s dispatch. Test mentions in commit message: '(tested: macOS)' or '(tested: Windows)'.

recurringPatterns.name: Correct pattern exists but new code uses old pattern
recurringPatterns.description: A correct solution exists (get_mtime, uname dispatch, deploy_managed_file) but new code written after the extraction uses the pre-extraction pattern. Extraction provides capability but not enforcement.
evidence: stat hooks vs get_mtime in check-lib.sh
harvest-session.sh paths vs workspace rule new paths
recurringPatterns.agentAction: Before writing platform-specific code, check if a helper exists in aitools-lib.sh or check-lib.sh.

recurringPatterns.name: Commit pipeline selectivity (commit gap)
recurringPatterns.description: During-session code changes get committed. End-of-session hook outputs do not. Session archives and harvested artifacts are stranded on the local machine.
evidence: v0.63.0 commit: only 2 files from 35-mission session
harvesting/ stale by 3 days
dotprofile untracked session files
recurringPatterns.structuralFix: NOT YET IMPLEMENTED. Decision #1 (auto-commit/push) is the designed fix. Highest-priority pipeline fix.
recurringPatterns.agentAction: Manually commit harvesting/ and session archives before ending sessions. Surface decision #1 urgency.

recurringPatterns.name: Cross-machine state divergence
recurringPatterns.description: Work on one machine creates decisions and artifacts not fully committed/pushed. Other machine operates on stale baseline. Divergence invisible until machine switch + Lagebeurteilung.
evidence: Mac 3/19-3/22 work not on Windows
Per-session estimates on Mac but not Windows
Dashboard architecture decided on Mac with S1 but not in repo
recurringPatterns.agentAction: At session start on a new machine, always do a Lagebeurteilung — assess what may have changed since the last session on this machine.

recurringPatterns.name: Demonstrate-then-skip
recurringPatterns.description: Agent demonstrates correct behavior (assessment, checklist, verification) at one boundary then skips it at the next. The correct pattern is known and recently executed — the skip is urgency overriding discipline.
evidence: Session 77a33baf: pre-commit checklist done, then straight to execution without Lagebeurteilung
RnTOD5XJFi: read files then jumped to editing hooks
S3-Golf: told to read code, skipped
Dashboard in prompts but never tested
recurringPatterns.structuralFix: Approaching structural fix threshold (decision #35: 3+ occurrences → structural fix). Intent sentinel hook designed but not deployed.
recurringPatterns.agentAction: After EVERY lifecycle transition (not just the first), pause and assess: What did I just decide? What am I about to do? Have I checked the terrain?

recurringPatterns.name: 6-stage carry-forward pipeline
recurringPatterns.description: Carry-forward is not 'commit and push' — it is 6 stages: (1) Produce, (2) Commit, (3) Push, (4) Pull, (5) Deploy, (6) Verify. Each stage has independent failure modes. Failures observed at stages 2, 4, 5, and 6.
evidence: Stage 2: selective commit (P3)
Stage 4: dotprofile dirty tree blocks pull
Stage 5: hooks crash, deploy scripts silent failure
Stage 6: no Lagebeurteilung on machine switch
recurringPatterns.agentAction: When assessing carry-forward, check all 6 stages — not just 'is it committed?'

recurringPatterns.name: Assumption propagation through agent chains
recurringPatterns.description: False claims propagate when verifiers check documents not code. Three verifiers all trusted upstream — chain-of-trust failure.
evidence: Agent #29 false claim about scratch persistence → 5 artifacts → 3 verifiers
.gitignore fix claimed but not executed → M19 and RECON-FRAGORD
Dashboard miss: 3 rounds of prompts missed shipped code
recurringPatterns.agentAction: Never trust upstream claims without reading the actual code or file. Mark unverifiable claims as ASSUMPTION.

recurringPatterns.name: Governance-focused analysis misses implementation
recurringPatterns.description: When tasked with analyzing the harness, agents focus on governance artifacts (rules, decisions, frameworks) and miss implementation (code, hooks, scripts, dashboard).
evidence: v1-v3 artifact intent was governance-only
Three rounds of prompts missed the dashboard
S3-Golf wrote CLAUDE.md from governance only, ignoring code
recurringPatterns.structuralFix: Four-pillar artifact intent (D-CODE-IS-HARNESS). Phase 2 code reading in mission prompts.
recurringPatterns.agentAction: When asked about the harness, always check: 'Did I read the code? Did I check scripts/? shared/hooks/? The dashboard?'

recurringPatterns.name: Context rot on user intent
recurringPatterns.description: After ~100K+ tokens of reading, the original user instruction gets buried. Agent drifts from research to execution without permission.
evidence: Session KHGOmVeNNM: agent jumped from research to editing hooks
General pattern: objectives buried under accumulated context
recurringPatterns.structuralFix: Intent sentinel hook designed (not deployed). Recency weight principle.
recurringPatterns.agentAction: After every 5+ Read calls, re-read the mission objective. Before transitioning from reading to writing, verify you have permission.

recurringPatterns.name: Behavioral framing gap
recurringPatterns.description: Content present in context has zero behavioral weight unless framed as 'what you should DO'. CC /resume loses operative weight via compression.
evidence: Dashboard in prompts but never tested — framed as 'what was built' not 'what you should use'
/resume compresses tool results, losing behavioral framing
recurringPatterns.structuralFix: /aitool-resume skill (RFC v7) with chronological transcript walk and boundary detection.
recurringPatterns.agentAction: When producing context for other agents, frame capabilities as actions: 'Launch the dashboard by...' not 'A dashboard was built.'

metaLessons.lesson: Recency weight is the governing principle for content conflicts
metaLessons.description: When instructions conflict, the most recent one carries the most weight. The commander's most recent prompt is always the highest-priority instruction. This applies to everything: files vs conversation, old rules vs new decisions, prior session vs current session.

metaLessons.lesson: Treat all static files as assumptions until verified
metaLessons.description: Everything in files — including this one — may be stale. Context (the live conversation) overrides files. When static content and context conflict, context wins.
metaLessons.source: nobul-ops CLAUDE.md principle, reinforced across 4 sessions

metaLessons.description: Claude Code sessions have 1M context. Subagents have 1M context. Read full files. Load complete rules. No token-based decisions.

metaLessons.lesson: Subagents are blank slates — inherit NOTHING
metaLessons.description: Subagents do not inherit rules, CLAUDE.md, skills context, or any project knowledge. Every delegation must include all needed context. The delegation cost is real but non-negotiable.
metaLessons.source: CC version dep #5, commander directive, OL-O12

metaLessons.description: Explore agents cannot Write or Edit. Work product dies with the agent. Always use general-purpose agents with explicit instructions and write permissions.
metaLessons.source: Commander directive (session 5HyCwPtSDH), blocked by block-claude-code-guide.sh hook

metaLessons.lesson: UCIs (coaching items) are ineffective for recurring patterns
metaLessons.description: Only structural fixes (hooks, scripts, rules) work for recurring behavioral patterns. Commander rejected UCI as 'weak sauce' after 3rd occurrence of same pattern. Decision #35 codifies: 3+ occurrences → structural fix.

metaLessons.lesson: The file you produce IS the harness
metaLessons.description: Every word in harness state documents has behavioral consequences. Inaccuracies propagate through agent chains. An incorrect claim about a hook becomes an incorrect modification by the next agent.

metaLessons.lesson: Re-read the mission objective before every major action
metaLessons.description: The commander's most repeated instruction across 4 sessions. After extensive reading (100K+ tokens), the original objective gets buried. Stop. Re-read. Then act.
metaLessons.source: Commander (15+ repetitions across sessions), OL-P9 (context rot)

metaLessons.lesson: Audit shipped capabilities, not just decisions
metaLessons.description: Three rounds of prompt design missed the dashboard — a major shipped capability — because analysts only looked at decisions and rules. Check CODE: scripts/, shared/hooks/, the dashboard, the deploy pipeline.

The observation-to-fact pipeline — observe, classify, verify, correct — is the primary work product. Code changes, config fixes, and feature builds are outputs of the discipline. A session's value is measured by its process artifacts quality, not just its code artifacts.
